final_prompt:
Can you help me write an email to my landlord saying I didn't owe that late fee? Thanks!

<document>
From: Dana Whitfield, Maple Court Apartments
Subject: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi,

Our records show this month's rent was received on the 3rd. As you know, rent is due
on the 1st, so a late fee of $75 has been added to your account. We were disappointed
to see this, since on-time payments help us keep the building running for everyone.
We'd appreciate it if you could be more careful going forward. Please pay the fee
along with next month's rent.

Thanks for understanding,
Dana

---
Lease excerpt (Maple Court residential lease):
Section 4.1: Rent is $1,450 per month, payable by check, money order, or the resident
portal.
Section 4.2: Rent is due on the 1st. A grace period applies through the 5th; no late
fees may be charged during the grace period.
Section 4.3: Returned payments incur a $35 fee.
Section 9.4: Notices to the landlord must be in writing and may be sent by email.
</document>

runs.answer:
Based on the lease, the $75 late fee appears to be improper, and you should dispute it.

**Why the fee conflicts with the lease:**
- Section 4.2 says rent is due on the 1st, with a grace period through the 5th, and that **no late fees may be charged during the grace period**.
- Your rent was received on the 3rd, which falls within that grace period. The landlord's own email acknowledges the payment date, so the fee isn't supported by the lease.

**What you can do:**
1. **Reply in writing (email works under Section 9.4).** A short, polite message is enough, for example:

   > Hi Dana,
   >
   > Thank you for your message regarding the $75 late fee for Unit 3B. Under Section 4.2 of my lease, rent is due on the 1st with a grace period through the 5th, and no late fees may be charged during the grace period. My rent was received on the 3rd, so I don't believe the fee applies. Please remove the $75 charge from my account and confirm in writing.
   >
   > Thank you,
   > [Your name], Unit 3B

2. **Keep records.** Save your proof of payment (receipt, bank statement, or portal confirmation showing the date) and this email thread.

3. **Don't pay the fee with next month's rent without noting the dispute.** If you do pay, write "paid under protest, disputed per Lease §4.2" on the payment or in the portal note so paying doesn't count as agreeing to the charge.

4. **If they refuse,** you can escalate to your local tenant rights organization, a housing counselor, or small claims court. Many jurisdictions also have rules limiting late fees, which may give you additional leverage. A local tenant union can confirm the rules where you live.

If you tell me your city or state, I can point out any local late-fee rules that might also apply.
